scope: Production-readiness review of every project in the canonical Bittrees project registry.

priorityDefinitions.P0: Launch blocker or material safety/reliability defect.
priorityDefinitions.P1: Required for a professional production release.
priorityDefinitions.P2: Important post-launch quality, reach, or maintainability improvement.

statusDefinitions.todo: Accepted into the backlog but not yet started.
statusDefinitions.in-progress: Implementation or evidence collection is active.
statusDefinitions.blocked: Cannot complete until a named decision, approval, dependency, or authority is available.
statusDefinitions.done: Every acceptance criterion has durable evidence and owner review recorded completion.

methodology.completionRule: A task is complete only when every acceptance criterion has durable evidence in the project repository, deployment, or approved operating record. Self-attestation alone is insufficient for security, legal, financial, or authority claims.
evidenceReviewed: README files, package scripts, tests, CI and release metadata
live public routes, HTTP metadata, security headers, discovery artifacts, and responsive layouts
IDACC project catalog and project planning context

limitations: This is a point-in-time technical and product review, not a legal opinion, financial audit, or independent smart-contract audit.
Private infrastructure, secrets, off-repository operating procedures, and third-party dashboards were not treated as complete without public-safe durable evidence.
Live deployments may lag their repositories; deployed smoke tests remain required after each release.

projects.evidenceSummary: The portal has a strong tested MCP and discovery foundation, but public indexing and write workflows intentionally remain gated while durable storage, approvals, and production operations are incomplete.

tasks.title: Move review workflows to an approved durable control plane
acceptanceCriteria: Registrations, claims, submissions, reviews, feedback, idempotency records, rate limits, audit events, and outbox delivery survive restarts and concurrent instances.
Migration, backup, restore, retention, and failure-recovery tests run against the production-class store.

tasks.title: Record source, security, legal, and operations launch approvals
acceptanceCriteria: Named owners approve the public source set, supported claims, threat model, incident plan, and indexing switch in a durable record.
The launch gate and robots policy are changed only by the reviewed release containing those approvals.

tasks.title: Publish approved Terms, privacy policy, and contact routes
acceptanceCriteria: Legal-approved Terms and privacy text identify the responsible entity, jurisdiction, data handling, retention, and user rights.
A monitored security, privacy, and support contact is linked from every page and machine contract.

tasks.title: Prove the complete agent contribution lifecycle
acceptanceCriteria: Automated tests cover registration through reviewed completion, rejection, feedback, duplicate requests, timeouts, and recovery.
At least two external MCP clients pass the same production smoke suite without gaining downstream mutation authority.

tasks.title: Complete MCP interoperability and discovery publication
acceptanceCriteria: MCP initialization, resources, tools, errors, CORS, conditional requests, and advertised MIME types pass conformance tests from the deployed origin.
The server package is submitted to appropriate registries only after experimental metadata and ownership are reviewed.

tasks.title: Establish production monitoring, SLOs, backups, and incident response
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboards and alerts cover availability, latency, error rate, queue depth, stale sources, failed delivery, and security events.
An on-call owner completes a documented restore and incident-response exercise.

projects.evidenceSummary: The accounting application is polished and has substantial contract testing, but its own milestone remains pre-mainnet and its live discovery, security headers, and operational evidence are incomplete.

tasks.title: Finish and refresh the Sepolia acceptance milestone
acceptanceCriteria: Deployer configuration, hosted validation, production role assignments, and the browser checklist are completed with evidence.
The overdue readiness status and projected launch date are replaced by a current owner-approved decision.

tasks.title: Independently review contracts, upgrades, and privileged roles
acceptanceCriteria: An independent review covers accounting invariants, role boundaries, upgrade authority, pause and recovery paths.
All critical and high findings are closed, retested, and linked from the release record.

tasks.title: Add deployed ledger write/readback acceptance tests
acceptanceCriteria: Hosted tests create, authorize, record, reconcile, and read back representative ledger events on the approved network.
Failure, retry, duplicate, wrong-chain, and revoked-role cases are verified.

tasks.title: Approve a mainnet rollout and rollback runbook
acceptanceCriteria: The runbook pins addresses, owners, role grants, verification steps, monitoring, pause conditions, and rollback decisions.
A second operator rehearses and signs off on the procedure.

tasks.title: Harden the public application and discovery surface
acceptanceCriteria: The deployed origin has a restrictive CSP, nosniff, clickjacking, referrer, and permissions policies.
Canonical, robots, sitemap, health, llms.txt, and an agent-readable product/API description return correct content types.

tasks.title: Provide professional onboarding, demo data, support, and disclosures
acceptanceCriteria: A read-only demo explains core accounting workflows before wallet connection.
Support, privacy, terms, network, preview-state, and financial-risk disclosures are visible and accessible.

projects.evidenceSummary: A live mainnet-facing product exists, but mobile overflow, absent CI evidence, transaction-risk validation, operational freshness, discovery, and policy surfaces keep it below production quality.

tasks.title: Remove mobile horizontal overflow and clipped financial data
acceptanceCriteria: Every route fits 320–430px viewports without horizontal scrolling or truncated balances, controls, charts, and transaction details.
Automated responsive screenshots and overflow assertions run in CI.

tasks.title: Prove transaction safety for swaps, approvals, liquidity, and lending
acceptanceCriteria: Simulation and E2E tests cover chain selection, token/address verification, allowance scope, slippage, min-out, reverts, and stale quotes.
High-risk actions show a human-readable preview and require an explicit final confirmation.

tasks.title: Create a protected main release pipeline
acceptanceCriteria: Pull requests and main run build, typecheck, tests, dependency checks, and deployed smoke tests.
Production releases are traceable to an immutable commit with rollback instructions.

tasks.title: Monitor portfolio snapshot freshness and provider health
acceptanceCriteria: Health output exposes last successful snapshot, source/network coverage, degradation, and safe-to-display state without secrets.
Alerts and recovery tests cover cron failure, RPC exhaustion, stale pricing, and provider failover.

tasks.title: Publish secure web metadata and agent-readable contracts
acceptanceCriteria: The root response includes production security headers, canonical metadata, robots, and a real sitemap.
llms.txt and a versioned read-only data/API contract distinguish observations from transaction actions.

tasks.title: Approve wallet, financial-risk, privacy, and preview-state disclosures
acceptanceCriteria: Reviewed terms identify entity, jurisdiction, non-custodial behavior, data handling, financial risk, and support contacts.
Every action accurately labels network, asset, contract, fees, and whether the feature is preview or production.

projects.evidenceSummary: The governance application exposes its mission and integrations, but the public page has weak hierarchy and lacks CI evidence, security headers, integration E2E coverage, discovery artifacts, and clear privacy controls.

tasks.title: Rebuild the landing hierarchy around governance tasks
acceptanceCriteria: Every page has one descriptive H1, concise task-first sections, and clear proposal, vote, forum, and contributor calls to action.
Mobile users can reach core actions without navigating a wall of mission copy.

tasks.title: Enforce the existing release gate in CI
acceptanceCriteria: Protected pull requests run build, typecheck, unit tests, dependency checks, and deployed smoke tests.
A production release records commit, environment, integration versions, approver, and rollback steps.

tasks.title: Test wallet, Snapshot, EAS, XMTP, and Push flows end to end
acceptanceCriteria: Tests cover successful and failed connection, signing, voting, attestation, message delivery, network mismatch, and provider outage.
No signature prompt or governance action is ambiguous about payload, network, or consequence.

tasks.title: Complete the contributor-application privacy and threat model
acceptanceCriteria: The review documents encryption, access control, key recovery, retention, deletion, logging, and abuse cases.
Negative tests prove unauthorized users and operators cannot read or alter protected applications.

tasks.title: Add production headers, metadata, and discovery
acceptanceCriteria: CSP, nosniff, clickjacking, referrer, permissions, canonical, robots, and a real sitemap are verified on the deployed origin.
llms.txt describes proposals, data sources, freshness, and which interactions require wallets or review.

tasks.title: Add integration monitoring, recovery, governance disclaimers, and support
acceptanceCriteria: Health and alerts cover Snapshot, RPC, messaging, attestation, and stale governance data with a rollback owner.
Approved privacy, terms, governance-effect, accessibility, and support information is linked from the application.

projects.evidenceSummary: The root Bittrees domain is live but functions as a very sparse three-link page. It does not yet present the full ecosystem or meet modern semantic, discovery, testing, and operational standards.

tasks.title: Replace the three-link page with the canonical Bittrees ecosystem hub
acceptanceCriteria: The site explains Bittrees clearly and lists every active product, data source, project stage, owner-approved description, and primary action.
agent.bittrees.org is the prominent AI-agent entry point and the directory is generated from shared registry data.

tasks.title: Deliver a professional responsive and accessible design system
acceptanceCriteria: Pages use main landmarks, a descriptive H1, keyboard-visible navigation, sufficient contrast, and useful mobile layouts.
Automated accessibility and responsive visual checks guard the shared layout.

tasks.title: Modernize the legacy frontend and establish CI
acceptanceCriteria: The supported toolchain passes lint, build, tests, dependency audit, and link validation on protected pull requests.
Deployments are immutable, observable, and reversible.

tasks.title: Publish complete security, canonical, and social metadata
acceptanceCriteria: Production headers include a restrictive CSP, nosniff, clickjacking, referrer, and permissions policies.
Canonical, favicon, descriptions, Open Graph, and structured organization/product metadata validate on every page.

tasks.title: Publish real crawl and AI discovery artifacts
acceptanceCriteria: robots.txt, sitemap.xml, llms.txt, and an ecosystem JSON feed return correct non-SPA content.
The feed points to canonical project resources and the unified MCP endpoint.

tasks.title: Assign content ownership, freshness checks, analytics, and support
acceptanceCriteria: Every ecosystem record has an owner, last-reviewed date, and automated broken-link/staleness check.
Privacy-respecting analytics, performance budgets, uptime monitoring, and a monitored contact route are documented.
tasks.progressNote: September 5: content freshness/link checks and build budgets are prepared for review. Completion awaits named content owners, a monitored support contact, and notification/uptime acceptance.

projects.evidenceSummary: The member application is functional and tested locally, but its gate experience, CI/release evidence, privacy model, integration freshness, discovery boundaries, and production operations need completion.

tasks.title: Prove the membership NFT gate and authorization lifecycle
acceptanceCriteria: E2E tests cover eligible, ineligible, transferred, revoked, wrong-network, stale-cache, provider-failure, and reconnect cases.
Protected content and APIs fail closed without leaking member data or private metadata.

tasks.title: Improve the pre-auth verification and recovery experience
acceptanceCriteria: Verification states explain what is checked, why, how long it may take, and how to retry or get support.
Slow wallet and provider paths never leave users on an indefinite uninformative screen.

tasks.title: Run the release gate and deployed member smoke suite in CI
acceptanceCriteria: Protected pull requests run lint, typecheck, unit tests, build, dependency checks, and gate negative tests.
Release metadata, environment, approver, deployed smoke evidence, and rollback instructions stay current.

tasks.title: Approve member-content privacy, retention, and access controls
acceptanceCriteria: A reviewed policy covers member identifiers, research content, messages, analytics, encryption, retention, deletion, and legal basis.
Access logs and negative authorization tests are available without exposing sensitive member content.

tasks.title: Monitor governance, token, messaging, and research-data freshness
acceptanceCriteria: Health output and alerts distinguish fresh, stale, degraded, and unavailable sources.
Operators have tested retry, cache invalidation, provider failover, and rollback procedures.

tasks.title: Publish public discovery without exposing member-only content
acceptanceCriteria: Canonical, robots, sitemap, security headers, and llms.txt describe only approved public capabilities and data boundaries.
The public agent manifest sends protected interactions through explicit authentication and review gates.

projects.evidenceSummary: The available canonical checkout has no committed history and the repository has no active deployment or CI evidence. Mainnet transaction intent raises a high safety bar before any relaunch.

tasks.title: Decide whether to archive or relaunch Bittrees Vault
acceptanceCriteria: An accountable owner records the supported product scope, network, integrations, users, maintenance commitment, and archive/relaunch decision.
The portal and repository communicate the decision consistently.

tasks.title: Establish a canonical committed and protected source history
acceptanceCriteria: Reviewed source is committed to the canonical repository with authorship, license, branch protection, and secret scanning.
A clean checkout builds reproducibly from documented prerequisites.

tasks.title: Verify all mainnet contracts, assets, authorities, and economic assumptions
acceptanceCriteria: Pinned addresses, bytecode, owners, upgradeability, fee tiers, decimals, liquidity assumptions, and supported chains are independently verified.
Unsupported or removed routes cannot be invoked from UI or code.

tasks.title: Add transaction simulation and adversarial E2E tests
acceptanceCriteria: Tests cover swaps, pool creation, allowances, slippage, price impact, wrong chain, token ordering, reverts, stale quotes, and partial failures.
Every write shows a verified human-readable preview before wallet confirmation.

tasks.title: Create CI, deployment, monitoring, and incident controls
acceptanceCriteria: CI runs lint, build, unit, integration, dependency, contract, and deployed smoke checks.
A public deployment, health check, alerts, pause owner, and rollback procedure are documented and exercised.

tasks.title: Complete disclosures, support, and agent discovery
acceptanceCriteria: Approved terms explain non-custodial behavior, transaction and liquidity risk, privacy, fees, networks, and support.
Canonical metadata, robots, sitemap, llms.txt, and read-only agent resources are published only after relaunch approval.

projects.evidenceSummary: The product and CI are comparatively mature, but its own release documentation keeps mainnet activation fail-closed until legal, security, auditor, operator, and durable-production gates are approved.

tasks.title: Record an explicit mainnet application activation decision
acceptanceCriteria: Verified manifests, networks, contracts, owners, operators, and release commit are approved in one immutable activation record.
The application remains fail-closed until every named hard gate is satisfied.

tasks.title: Complete independent escrow and marketplace security review
acceptanceCriteria: The audit covers escrow lifecycle, tokens, roles, settlement, disputes, upgrades, reentrancy, signatures, and abuse paths.
Critical and high findings are closed and the deployment operator signs the reviewed testnet acceptance record.

tasks.title: Prove durable marketplace persistence and recovery
acceptanceCriteria: Bounties, bids, evidence, reviews, disputes, and chain reconciliation use production migrations, backups, retention, and access controls.
A restore and disaster-recovery exercise meets documented recovery objectives.

tasks.title: Approve marketplace Terms, AUP, privacy, entity, and jurisdiction
acceptanceCriteria: Counsel-approved documents cover marketplace role, escrow, disputes, prohibited work, privacy, taxes, sanctions, and jurisdiction.
Versioned acceptance and policy-change records are retained.

tasks.title: Test multichain settlement, wallet sessions, and moderator abuse cases
acceptanceCriteria: E2E tests cover create, fund, submit, accept, dispute, cancel, refund, settle, reorg, wrong chain, and provider failure.
Wallet auth, CSRF, replay, session expiry, role escalation, and moderator actions have negative tests and audit logs.

tasks.title: Expose safe agent contracts and production telemetry
acceptanceCriteria: llms.txt and versioned APIs distinguish read-only discovery, review queues, and wallet/onchain actions, and connect to the universal portal.
Health, SLO, release, queue, indexer, and settlement metrics are monitored with an incident owner.

projects.evidenceSummary: Chirpy has a polished web experience and recurring protocol checks, but durable production services, signed desktop releases, final branding, privacy/moderation controls, metadata, and operational proof remain unfinished.

tasks.title: Provision and validate the production gate, environment, and durable services
acceptanceCriteria: Production auth/gating, data stores, secrets, network providers, retention, backups, and access controls are configured and documented.
The deployment fails closed when required services or environment values are unavailable.

tasks.title: Cut the first signed and update-safe desktop release
acceptanceCriteria: macOS, Windows, and supported Linux artifacts are reproducible, signed where applicable, checksummed, malware-scanned, and linked to release notes.
Install, upgrade, downgrade/recovery, deep-link, and update-authority tests pass on supported platforms.

tasks.title: Replace interim icons and finish the cross-platform brand system
acceptanceCriteria: Final approved icons, app metadata, install screens, empty states, and social assets render crisply on every target.
Automated visual checks prevent placeholder assets from returning.

tasks.title: Approve messaging privacy, encryption, retention, and moderation controls
acceptanceCriteria: Documentation accurately explains protocol encryption, metadata visibility, local/server storage, retention, deletion, blocking, reporting, and operator access.
Terms, privacy, moderation, abuse response, and contact paths are reviewed and versioned.

tasks.title: Test messaging and token-gate recovery across clients
acceptanceCriteria: Web and desktop tests cover XMTP, Push, token gates, offline sync, reconnect, duplicate delivery, revoked access, wrong network, and provider outages.
A user can recover safely from partial initialization without losing locally controlled data.

tasks.title: Complete web discovery, security headers, health, and support operations
acceptanceCriteria: Description, canonical, robots, sitemap, CSP, nosniff, clickjacking, referrer, and permissions metadata validate on the live origin.
llms.txt documents safe read-only capabilities while health, SLOs, backups, provider degradation, and incident ownership are monitored.

projects.evidenceSummary: The source-maintained directory has solid static verification and publication scripts, but no canonical public product URL, continuous main release, freshness/moderation SLA, professional UI evidence, or agent-facing feed.

tasks.title: Deploy a stable canonical public directory
acceptanceCriteria: A production domain serves an immutable verified build and the canonical registry points to it.
DNS, TLS, hosting ownership, rollback, uptime, and deployed smoke checks are documented.

tasks.title: Define and enforce source verification and freshness SLAs
acceptanceCriteria: Every entry records source URLs, verifier, verification date, status, and expiry/review deadline.
Automated checks quarantine stale, unreachable, conflicting, or unsupported records before publication.

tasks.title: Publish contribution, moderation, correction, and takedown workflows
acceptanceCriteria: Submission and change history identify reviewer, evidence, decision, conflicts, and appeal path.
Anti-spam, trademark, impersonation, correction, and takedown policies have accountable owners.

tasks.title: Automate protected main and monthly IPFS/ENS releases
acceptanceCriteria: Main CI runs schema, links, freshness, build, accessibility, dependency, and deployed smoke checks.
Monthly artifacts pin immutable content identifiers and prove ENS update, rollback, and signer review.

tasks.title: Ship a searchable, accessible, and attributable directory interface
acceptanceCriteria: Users can search, filter, sort, inspect verification evidence, report problems, and use the site by keyboard and mobile.
Performance and accessibility budgets are enforced in CI.

tasks.title: Publish versioned JSON, llms.txt, provenance, and usage terms
acceptanceCriteria: A stable machine feed exposes schema version, provenance, freshness, pagination, license, and correction routes.
Canonical metadata and llms.txt link the feed to the unified Bittrees MCP resource catalog.

projects.evidenceSummary: IDACC is the most mature released product in the set, with signed artifacts and a security-conscious architecture, but version messaging, cross-platform release proof, recovery drills, runtime security, support, and discovery need tightening.

tasks.title: Reconcile README, installed, website, and latest release versions
acceptanceCriteria: The repository, site, in-app updater, release feed, and installed-app status identify current, supported, and latest versions from one source of truth.
Stale versions cannot be presented as current after a release.

tasks.title: Automate signed cross-platform install and update acceptance
acceptanceCriteria: Supported macOS, Windows, and Linux artifacts pass clean install, launch, update, rollback/recovery, signature, checksum, and malware checks.
Release provenance is generated by protected CI from the tagged commit.

tasks.title: Exercise workspace backup, restore, migration, and downgrade recovery
acceptanceCriteria: Documented drills restore projects, agent state, settings, logs, and credentials with safe redaction and clear recovery objectives.
Interrupted upgrade and schema migration tests cannot silently corrupt user work.

tasks.title: Audit Manager, IPC, plugins, model routing, and local execution boundaries
acceptanceCriteria: Threat modeling and tests cover untrusted project content, prompt injection, shell/process execution, IPC, plugin permissions, path traversal, secrets, logs, and update authority.
Critical and high findings are fixed and independently retested.

tasks.title: Publish support, privacy, diagnostics, and lifecycle expectations
acceptanceCriteria: Users can find supported platforms, data locations, telemetry behavior, diagnostic redaction, deletion, backup, and contact information.
Troubleshooting and safe-mode guidance covers failed agents, corrupted workspaces, update failures, and credential rotation.

tasks.title: Expose release metadata for agents and complete accessibility QA
acceptanceCriteria: llms.txt and a versioned release/support JSON feed link to checksums, compatibility, changelog, and the unified portal.
Keyboard, screen-reader, zoom, contrast, reduced-motion, and cross-platform UI checks are part of release acceptance.
tasks.progressNote: September 5: website release/support feed, agent guide, and keyboard/reduced-motion improvements are prepared for review. Browser, screen-reader, desktop, and deployed-route acceptance remain outstanding.

projects.evidenceSummary: The public origin is password-protected and the repository describes build-ready scaffolding rather than a production service. Backend, contracts, indexer, environment, audit, CI, recovery, legal, and public discovery gates remain.

tasks.title: Decide and document the preview gate and public launch path
acceptanceCriteria: An owner records who may access the protected preview, what is safe to test, the exit criteria, and the public launch decision.
Health and discovery endpoints expose only approved public-safe status while the gate remains.

tasks.title: Provision production IPFS, database, indexer, contracts, and environment
acceptanceCriteria: Pinned network and contract manifests, RPC/indexer configuration, admin roles, treasury destination, storage, migrations, and secrets are reviewed and reproducible.
The application fails closed when any authoritative dependency is absent or stale.

tasks.title: Complete populated Sepolia end-to-end acceptance
acceptanceCriteria: Tests cover create, upload, mint, profile, collection, list, buy, offer, cancel, moderation, indexing, royalties, reorg, wrong chain, and provider failure.
The acceptance record includes verified artifacts, data population, browser/device results, operators, and unresolved risks.

tasks.title: Close dependency risk and complete contract, admin, upload, and marketplace review
acceptanceCriteria: Independent review covers contracts, roles, upgrades, signatures, marketplace settlement, file handling, content abuse, authentication, and secrets.
Critical/high findings and launch-blocking dependency advisories are fixed and retested.

tasks.title: Establish a green protected release and recovery pipeline
acceptanceCriteria: Main CI runs build, tests, schema/migrations, audit, contract checks, and deployed smoke tests from a clean source tree.
Database/IPFS backup, restore, indexer replay, monitoring, moderation escalation, and rollback exercises are documented.

tasks.title: Publish professional metadata, agent contracts, policies, and support
acceptanceCriteria: After launch approval, the site exposes canonical metadata, robots, sitemap, llms.txt, versioned read APIs, health, and universal MCP links.
Approved Terms, privacy, creator rights, royalties, marketplace risk, moderation, takedown, and support policies are versioned and visible.

projects.evidenceSummary: SkillMesh has the strongest project-level agent discovery surface, including MCP, OpenAPI, A2A, llms.txt, health, and a manifest. Production runtime, network decisions, contract/security evidence, external conformance, release operations, and mobile information density remain.

tasks.title: Link and complete the existing discovery surface
acceptanceCriteria: Root HTML advertises MCP, OpenAPI, A2A, agent manifest, and llms.txt with correct types, canonical metadata, favicon, and a real sitemap.
All discovery documents share canonical version, environment, network, ownership, and capability identifiers.

tasks.title: Prove MCP, A2A, and OpenAPI interoperability externally
acceptanceCriteria: A client matrix validates authentication, discovery, schemas, errors, streaming, pagination, timeouts, retries, and version negotiation.
Conformance runs against the deployed origin and prevents contract drift between protocols.

tasks.title: Provision and monitor the production provider runtime
acceptanceCriteria: Provider execution, queues, storage, secrets, billing/settlement dependencies, rate limits, and fail-closed behavior are production configured.
SLOs, load tests, alerts, backups, recovery, and incident ownership meet the published service contract.

tasks.title: Approve the testnet-to-production network and contract security plan
acceptanceCriteria: Owners record whether launch remains Sepolia or moves networks, with verified contracts, roles, upgrades, pause, settlement, and migration steps.
Independent review closes critical/high contract, identity, payment, and authorization findings.

tasks.title: Secure executable skills and content-addressed artifacts
acceptanceCriteria: Sandboxing, permissions, network/file/process access, resource limits, signatures, IPFS integrity, malware checks, revocation, and audit logs are threat-modeled and tested.
Untrusted skill metadata or output cannot escalate provider, user, wallet, or host authority.

tasks.title: Complete settlement E2E, protected releases, and mobile information architecture
acceptanceCriteria: Identity, publish, discover, execute, meter, pay, dispute, revoke, and recover flows pass deployed E2E tests with release provenance and rollback.
The long mobile page is reorganized into task-first progressive disclosure with performance and accessibility budgets.

projects.evidenceSummary: The public site is visually polished and content-rich, but it is extremely long on mobile and lacks CI evidence, robust lead capture, independently versioned methodology, legal/commercial review, service monitoring, and agent-readable data.

tasks.title: Create a protected test, build, deploy, and smoke pipeline
acceptanceCriteria: Pull requests and main run lint, tests, build, accessibility, links, dependency checks, performance budgets, and deployed smoke tests.
Production releases are immutable, approved, monitored, and reversible.

tasks.title: Shorten and restructure the very long mobile experience
acceptanceCriteria: Priority audiences can reach site-screening, partner, investor, and contact actions through concise navigation and progressive disclosure.
Mobile performance, reading length, layout, keyboard use, contrast, and reduced motion meet documented budgets.

tasks.title: Replace browser-only email handoff with reliable consented lead intake
acceptanceCriteria: A server-backed workflow validates submissions, records consent, limits abuse, routes to an accountable owner, and sends auditable acknowledgements.
Privacy, retention, deletion, CRM access, failure recovery, and spam controls are documented and tested.

tasks.title: Independently validate and version energy and economic methodology
acceptanceCriteria: Every material estimate states inputs, units, date, geography, source, assumptions, uncertainty, exclusions, and calculation version.
An independent reviewer signs the methodology and automated regression fixtures protect published calculations.

tasks.title: Review commercial claims, LOI workflow, privacy, and jurisdiction
acceptanceCriteria: Approved copy distinguishes estimates, targets, offers, commitments, regulatory assumptions, and non-binding materials.
Terms, privacy, entity, jurisdiction, consent, contact, and LOI handling are versioned and visible.

tasks.title: Publish monitored agent-readable screening and offer data
acceptanceCriteria: llms.txt and a versioned read-only schema expose approved site-screening inputs, methodology, provenance, freshness, and limitations through the unified portal.
Health, analytics, uptime, form delivery, stale data, and incident ownership are monitored without leaking submitted lead data.
